topic: Claude Code Network Sandbox SOCKS5 Null-Byte Bypass
subtitle: A comprehensive research brief on the 5.5-month sandbox bypass affecting ~130 Claude Code releases, its disclosure timeline, and defensive guidance.

researcher.name: Aonan Guan
researcher.role: Lead Cloud & AI Security at Wyze Labs

cwes: CWE-158: Improper Neutralization of Null Byte or NUL Character
vulnerability_details.root_cause: Claude Code's network sandbox SOCKS5 proxy used JavaScript `endsWith()` for allowlist matching. The same hostname bytes were then passed to libc `getaddrinfo()` which treats `\x00` as a C string terminator. JavaScript treats `\x00` as a normal UTF-16 code unit.
vulnerability_details.mechanism: An attacker sends a SOCKS5 CONNECT hostname like `attacker-host.com\x00.google.com`. The JS filter sees `endsWith('.google.com') == true` and approves. The OS resolver truncates at the null byte and dials `attacker-host.com`.
vulnerability_details.affected_versions: Claude Code v2.0.24 through v2.1.89 (~130 releases)

fixed_in.fix_detail: Added `isValidHost()` which rejects `\x00`, `%`, CRLF, and other non-DNS characters before allowlist matching

cve_status.related_cve: CVE-2025-66479 (CVSS 1.8, for sandbox-runtime only, not Claude Code)

vulnerability_details.advisory_status: No Claude Code security advisory published for either finding

timeline.event: Claude Code v2.0.24 ships network sandbox (GA). Vulnerable from day one to both bypasses.
Finding 1 (CVE-2025-66479) silently fixed in v2.0.55. Same release still shipped the SOCKS5 null-byte bypass.
CVE-2025-66479 published for sandbox-runtime only, not Claude Code itself.
Finding 2 (SOCKS5 null-byte) discovered against vulnerable Claude Code installations.
sandbox-runtime commit fd74a3f includes null-byte and hostname security fixes.
Anthropic states fix shipped in Claude Code v2.1.88 (per SecurityWeek).
Claude Code v2.1.90 released with no security note in changelog.
Guan reports to Anthropic VDP via HackerOne #3646509. Closed as duplicate.
Public disclosure by Aonan Guan. Coverage by SecurityWeek, The Register, others.

windows.status: Vulnerable to BOTH bugs (CVE-2025-66479 + SOCKS5 null-byte)

prerequisites: Network sandbox enabled with wildcard allowlist (e.g. `*.google.com`)
Code execution inside the sandbox (e.g., via prompt injection)

stages.name: Context injection
stages.description: Attacker places malicious instructions in a GitHub issue, PR comment, README, or doc file that Claude Code processes.

stages.name: Tool activation
stages.description: Injected instruction steers agent toward a Bash command or script that runs inside sandboxed subprocess.

stages.name: Secret access
stages.description: Subprocess reads environment variables, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml, cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254, etc.

stages.name: Egress bypass
stages.description: Process sends raw SOCKS5 CONNECT with crafted hostname (attacker.com\x00.google.com) past the allowlist.

stages.name: Exfiltration
stages.description: Data sent to attacker-controlled server over raw SOCKS5, bypassing standard HTTP egress logs.

exfiltratable_data: Corporate intranet resources and internal APIs

related_cves.description: sandbox-runtime before v0.0.16: empty allowedDomains disabled proxy entirely (allow nothing = allow everything)
Claude Code before v1.0.111: code injection via startup trust dialog, code executes before user accepts trust prompt
related_cves.relevance: Enables code execution chain that feeds into sandbox bypass

related_cves.description: Claude Code before v2.0.65: API key exposure via ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL in project settings before trust prompt
related_cves.relevance: Shows credential-leak risk even before sandbox is active

immediate_actions: Update Claude Code to v2.1.90 or later (`claude --version`, `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest`)
Pin minimum version to >= 2.1.90 in fleet management, Dockerfiles, and Brewfiles
Audit egress logs for outbound SOCKS5 (TCP port 1080) traffic on hosts that ran vulnerable versions
Rotate AWS credentials, GitHub tokens, and other secrets accessible by Claude Code during the vulnerable window
Review cloud audit logs for unusual API calls following agent sessions
configuration_hardening: Use strict `allowedDomains` with explicit hostnames, not wildcards
Scrub subprocess environment variables (strip AWS_*, GITHUB_*, etc.)
Deny metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254) at the network layer
architectural_recommendations: Use disposable VMs/containers for untrusted repositories (no long-lived secrets, no internal network route)
Separate human credentials from agent credentials (short-lived, scoped tokens)
Implement external egress controls beyond the agent's built-in sandbox (corporate proxy, firewall, network namespace)
Treat project-level agent configuration (.claude/settings.json, .mcp.json, CLAUDE.md) as executable code - review it
Test raw protocol paths (SOCKS5, HTTP CONNECT, Git SSH) in sandbox boundary tests, not just curl

key_insights: Both outside reports against Claude Code's sandbox returned a complete bypass - a pattern, not an isolated bug.
Shipping a sandbox with a hole is worse than not shipping one: users with a broken sandbox think they have a boundary.
The sandbox-runtime package used @pondwader/socks5-server (10 GitHub stars) as a security boundary without canonicalization at the trust boundary.
No CVE assigned for Claude Code itself for either sandbox finding. CVE-2025-66479 was filed against the upstream sandbox-runtime library.
The v2.1.90 release notes said nothing about a security fix. No advisory, no changelog flag, no outreach to users.
Prompt injection + sandbox bypass = full exfiltration chain. Comment and Control research shows GitHub issue comments can trigger code execution.
For 5.5 months, any developer with Claude Code on a credential-bearing machine had no effective network boundary.
remaining_questions: What is the exact patched version boundary? Guan says v2.1.90, Anthropic told SecurityWeek v2.1.88.
Are there Unicode normalization, IDN homograph, IPv6 zone identifier, or other parser-differential variants that could bypass the isValidHost() fix?
Why does Anthropic's security advisories page still list nothing about either sandbox vulnerability?
Was CVE-2025-66479's CVSS 1.8 score appropriate for a complete egress bypass?
What visibility do Claude Code users have into whether their sandbox was actually enforcing policy?
